items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

ctx.x: Yes recapitulation. And I had to say this on an oral test at Bard College but I — maybe, probably as a kid I had dyslexia on reading, and now I have ear dyslexia. If I’m going to learn a language I can read it but I just had my record player on all the time in Springfield, Massachusetts and wherever, and later New York and here. And so I’ve missed many events of growing up. I just had to hear this record, “Scythian Suite” by Prokofiev, Shostakovich’s Tenth Symphony. I remember standing up at the Bushnell Memorial…

loud, and some guy behind me said, “Should I put some restraint on you?” But, and then Monk, how he ended “I Should Care.” Chris Connor’s version of “Driftwood” which nobody seems to play anymore. Abbey’s “Throw It Away,” “Down Here Below”, Mal Waldron “Straight Ahead.”

That’s certainly something for those moments. I had one where I was at a Mahavishnu Orchestra concert with John McLaughlin and Billy Cobham did something on the drums that made me like leap out of my seat. And I’m not prone to do that kind of thing.
